figures.caption: **Figure 1. Earth and its satellites, to scale.** Starlink hugs the planet like a thin line. The old kind of satellite internet, and GPS, sit far out.
figures.alt: Figure 1. Earth and its satellites, to scale. Starlink hugs the planet like a thin line. The old kind of satellite internet, and GPS, sit far out.

figures.caption: **Figure 2. The thin line in Figure 1, stretched out.** Now you can see where Starlink flies, next to the Space Station and the Hubble telescope.
figures.alt: Figure 2. The thin line in Figure 1, stretched out. Now you can see where Starlink flies, next to the Space Station and the Hubble telescope.

figures.caption: **Figure 3. The usual path from a house.** Dish to satellite to gateway, then on to the rest of the internet. Downloads take the same path in reverse.
figures.alt: Figure 3. The usual path from a house. Dish to satellite to gateway, then on to the rest of the internet. Downloads take the same path in reverse.

figures.caption: **Figure 4. The delay, Starlink against the old kind of satellite internet.** Starlink's bar is a sliver. The old kind is many times longer, because its satellites are so far away.
figures.alt: Figure 4. The delay, Starlink against the old kind of satellite internet. Starlink's bar is a sliver. The old kind is many times longer, because its satellites are so far away.

figures.caption: **Figure 5. The beam moves, the dish doesn't.** The beam follows satellites across the sky. Older rectangular dishes had a motor; the current ones don't.
figures.alt: Figure 5. The beam moves, the dish doesn't. The beam follows satellites across the sky. Older rectangular dishes had a motor; the current ones don't.

figures.caption: **Figure 6. The current dishes, side by side.** The small one is made for travel. The app tells you which one you have.
figures.alt: Figure 6. The current dishes, side by side. The small one is made for travel. The app tells you which one you have.

figures.caption: **Figure 7. Neighbors share the capacity overhead.** A drawing, not real speeds. The more people online at once, the smaller each share.
figures.alt: Figure 7. Neighbors share the capacity overhead. A drawing, not real speeds. The more people online at once, the smaller each share.

figures.caption: **Figure 8. Which plan works where.** A home plan works only at its home address. Roam works wherever Starlink has service when you park, and while driving on a dish made for it.
figures.alt: Figure 8. Which plan works where. A home plan works only at its home address. Roam works wherever Starlink has service when you park, and while driving on a dish made for it.

figures.caption: **Figure 9. One tree, repeated short drops.** The gray wedge is sky the tree hides. Each satellite that crosses it causes a short drop, then the next one takes over.
figures.alt: Figure 9. One tree, repeated short drops. The gray wedge is sky the tree hides. Each satellite that crosses it causes a short drop, then the next one takes over.

figures.caption: **Figure 10. Weather and your dish.** Heavy rain can cause short drops, and the dish heats itself to melt snow. Starlink says a cover makes things worse.
figures.alt: Figure 10. Weather and your dish. Heavy rain can cause short drops, and the dish heats itself to melt snow. Starlink says a cover makes things worse.

figures.caption: **Figure 11. Two networks in one house.** Your phone's speed is the slower of the two links. Test next to the router to see the Starlink link alone.
figures.alt: Figure 11. Two networks in one house. Your phone's speed is the slower of the two links. Test next to the router to see the Starlink link alone.

figures.caption: **Figure 12. Three ways to set up the Wi-Fi.** Starlink's router works on its own, but it won't join another brand's mesh. To use your own router, bypass mode turns Starlink's Wi-Fi off.
figures.alt: Figure 12. Three ways to set up the Wi-Fi. Starlink's router works on its own, but it won't join another brand's mesh. To use your own router, bypass mode turns Starlink's Wi-Fi off.

figures.caption: **Figure 13. Before you blame Starlink.** Test next to the router first. Fast there means the problem is inside, in your Wi-Fi. Slow there means checking the sky, the time, the weather and your plan.
figures.alt: Figure 13. Before you blame Starlink. Test next to the router first. Fast there means the problem is inside, in your Wi-Fi. Slow there means checking the sky, the time, the weather and your plan.
